title: What if your city
hit 60 °C?
ticker: SUNNY AND 22°  ·  BEAUTIFUL DAY IN NEW YORK  ·
HEAT ADVISORY IN EFFECT  ·  COOLING CENTERS OPEN  ·  DRINK WATER  ·
41°C  ·  HOTTEST DAY IN NEW YORK HISTORY  ·  STAY INDOORS  ·
EXTREME HEAT EMERGENCY  ·  STAY INDOORS  ·  CALL 911 IF SOMEONE COLLAPSES  ·
captions:
About 280,000 people walk through
here on a normal day.

Apple builds iPhones for up to 35 °C.
After that, they start to slow down.

Down in the subway it's worse.
One platform hit 40 °C on a 30 °C day.

New York's hottest day ever:
41 °C, in 1936. Broken.

Under the street,
power cables overheat.

Too hot for some jets. Phoenix
grounded regional planes at 48 °C.

Every air conditioner in Manhattan
is running at once.

In 2018, 42 °C killed 23,000 bats
in two days in Australia.

Hotter than the hottest temperature
ever reliably measured on Earth.

The world record, 56.7 °C
from 1913, is gone.

Then the heat breaks. The first
raindrops hit the road and boil.

items.label: AVERAGE ADULT · IN SHADE · NO WATER

endCard.fine: THIS IS FICTIONAL  ·  NEW YORK'S RECORD IS 41 °C (106 °F), SET IN 1936. IT HAS NEVER BEEN BROKEN.
